document_metadata.document_title: Flood Control and Water Quality Protection Manual

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Chapter 10 Water Quality sets post-construction BMP requirements for new development and redevelopment. Flood control detention and conveyance design use multi-frequency storms (including 100-year system capacity / street criteria; on-site detention to prevent increases for 1-, 10-, and 100-year peaks).
peak_flow_calculation_method: 100-year design storm for major drainage / easement containment

evidence.excerpt: A Stormwater Design Guide for Development in Springfield

City Flood Control and Water Quality Protection Manual
2-, 25-, and 100-year design flows / 1-, 10-, and 100-year storms

100-year (1 percent AEP) rainfall / on-site detention
stormwater detention / Best Management Practices (BMPs)
Therefore, the WQV is based on the runoff from a 1 inch rainfall.
evidence.page_or_section: Chapter 10, Section 2.1 Water Quality Volume, page 290

evidence.excerpt: Redevelopment projects where the previous development was not required to meet the water quality requirement shall meet a reduced WQV based on the runoff from a 0.5-inch rainfall
The required drain time for bioretention is 12-72 hours.
tf = maximum drain time (days) (use 3 days for the 72-hour max drain time requirement)
Bioretention storage should be located at least two feet above the seasonal high level of the water table.
Pervious pavement storage should be located at least two feet above the seasonal high level of the water table.

The bioretention soil mix filter bed thickness (df) shall be a minimum of 24 inches for pollutant removal and plant health in bioretention with an underdrain. The bioretention soil mix filter bed thickness (df) shall be a minimum of 12 inches for bioretention without an underdrain.
The preferred ponding depth is 12 inches and the maximum allowed is 18 inches.
The thickness of the rock storage shall be a minimum of 6 inches when no underdrain is used and 9 inches when an underdrain is used.
underdrains shall be provided if the existing subgrade infiltration rate is less than 0.5 inches/hour
In-service pervious pavement shall have a minimum infiltration rate of 10 inches/hour
To minimize the potential of algae growth, a minimum permanent pool depth of 6 feet must be provided.
designing a functional outlet to release the WQV over a 24-hour drain time is practically impossible
The basin length to width ratio should be between 2:1 and 4:1. The minimum allowable ratio is 1:1.
Design the outlet works to release the WQV in 22 to 28 hours.

Pollutant removal efficiency of the system shall be certified by an independent certification program including but not limited to: U.S. EPA Technology Verification Program, State of Washington Technology Assessment Protocol - Ecology (TAPE), the Technology Acceptance Reciprocity Partnership Protocol (TARP), New Jersey Corporation for Advance Technology (NJCAT) or the State of Maryland Proprietary Practice acceptance program.

design_parameters.mtd_verification_program: U.S. EPA Technology Verification Program; TAPE; TARP; NJCAT; Maryland Proprietary Practice acceptance program
design_parameters.enrich_notes: WQV uses 1-inch rainfall for new development; redevelopment may use 0.5-inch on redeveloped impervious area. Bioretention filter media minimum is 24 inches with underdrain. Rock storage minimum is 9 inches when underdrain is used. In-service pervious pavement minimum infiltration is 10 in/hr. Extended wet detention WQV drain time is approximately 12–15 hours. Constructed wetland WQV release is 22–28 hours; length:width recommended 2:1 to 4:1 (minimum 1:1).
